blocks.prompt: 10 Find the value of \(x\) and \(y\) if \((5 - 2i)(x + iy) + 3 = i(11 - i) - 4i\).
blocks.explanation:
Same type as Question 9.
We must find \(x\) and \(y\).
Plan: simplify the right side, move 3 across, expand, compare parts, and solve by elimination.
steps:
Given: \((5 - 2i)(x + iy) + 3 = i(11 - i) - 4i\), \(x, y\) real.
To find: \(x\) and \(y\).
Method: Bring both sides to (real) + (imaginary)\(i\) form, compare parts, solve the two linear equations.

Simplify the right side
\[i(11 - i) - 4i = 11i - i^2 - 4i\]
\[= 1 + 7i\]
Why: \(-i^2 = 1\) and \(11i - 4i = 7i\).

Move 3 to the right
\[(5 - 2i)(x + iy) = 1 + 7i - 3\]
\[= -2 + 7i\]
Why: Subtract 3 from both sides; 3 is real, so only the real part changes.

Expand the left side
\[(5 - 2i)(x + iy)\]
\[= 5x + 5iy - 2ix - 2i^2 y\]
\[= (5x + 2y) + (5y - 2x)i\]
Why: \(-2i^2 y = +2y\) is real.

Compare parts
\[5x + 2y = -2 \quad (1)\]
\[-2x + 5y = 7 \quad (2)\]
Why: Equality of complex numbers.

Eliminate \(x\)
\[2 \times (1): \; 10x + 4y = -4\]
\[5 \times (2): \; -10x + 25y = 35\]
\[\text{Add: } 29y = 31\]
\[y = \dfrac{31}{29}\]
Why: Making the \(x\) coefficients \(10\) and \(-10\) lets them cancel when we add.
